solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Big hit as wrecking ball taken to flats?

definitions.meaning: read literally: a thing that breaks up an apartment building

explanation.surface: A demolition crew swinging a wrecking ball into an apartment block, hailed as a big hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading; flats here are apartments, and a block of them is what gets busted.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a wartime bomb able to flatten a whole city block, the word moved on to mean any huge commercial success.

clue.text: Epsom Derby?

parts.note: the surface wants the Surrey racecourse; the setter uses it to mean English, as opposed to American
the surface wants the famous horse race; the setter means the American name for a round, hard felt hat

explanation.surface: A two-word reference to the famous English horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a flat race run at Epsom in Surrey. But Americans call the round hard hat a derby, and the English name for that same hat is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional-use definition: the hat called a derby in America is a bowler in England.

clue.text: Viva the dental check!

definitions.meaning: short for viva voce, a spoken exam, especially for a doctorate
the dentist's look inside the mouth

explanation.surface: A cheer for a trip to the dentist, as if a check-up deserved celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viva' looks like the Italian cheer; here it is the academic viva voce, an exam taken by speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a viva is examined by speech, and a dental check examines the mouth, both meanings of oral.

clue.text: Instrument contained spirit

parts.note: kettling is the police tactic of containing a crowd in a cordon

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that holds some kind of spirit inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: To kettle protesters is to hem them in, a term from British policing, which is why 'contained' is a past-tense verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the kettledrum, or timpani, is a percussion instrument shaped like a cauldron.

clue.text: State where odd bits lost in dust-bath

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh, are thrown away, and the even ones remain

parts.note: d-U-s-T-b-A-t-H: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A place where a bird's dust-bath has lost some bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen does not count as a letter; count only the eight letters of dust and bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Utah is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Fruity CEO?

parts.note: the surface wants an eccentric, colourful personality; the setter means a name made of fruit
the chief executive, the most senior person in a company

explanation.surface: A company chief with a colourful, perhaps eccentric, personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests a lively character, but the setter wants the slang phrase for a boss that happens to contain a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the slang for the most important person in an organisation is literally the highest fruit in the bunch.

clue.text: Scarlet concealer applied to fibre in makeover

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A cosmetics tip: scarlet concealer dabbed on as part of a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Concealer is a makeup product, which suits 'makeover', but here the scarlet word itself does the concealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym from marketing: giving a company a new name and look is a makeover of its image.

clue.text: Worker of wizardry perhaps in test of lexicographical knowledge?

parts.note: casting spells is one kind of wizardry, hence 'perhaps'
a worker is a type of bee in the hive

explanation.surface: A magician's assistant taking part in a word quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order is reversed: the worker comes first in the clue but last in the answer, as 'worker of wizardry' describes a bee that does magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the contest tests how well competitors can spell words, knowledge of the dictionary.

clue.text: Coastline that's rocky in parts

indicators.note: rocky also means unsteady, so the letters wobble out of their order

explanation.surface: A shore that is rocky only in some stretches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' fits a coastline so naturally that it hides its job as the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something sectional is made of, or divided into, separate sections.

clue.text: Primitive — as an aristocrat?

definitions.meaning: from the first stage of development
an invented adjective: a peer's title plus -Y, the way 'lordly' means like a lord

explanation.surface: A jibe that aristocrats are primitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark licenses the made-up word: EARL-Y, behaving like an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means belonging to an early stage; the second sense is a pun on the title earl.

clue.text: Crumb also coloured red

indicators.note: to colour a story is to distort it, so the letters are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crumb that has also been dyed red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' reads as the colour of the crumb, but it is a noun here: a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lambrusco is a sparkling Italian wine, usually red.

clue.text: American author, one with French post?

parts.note: a Norman comes from Normandy in France
to post is to mail, and one who does it is a mailer
turns 'post' into a person: someone who deals in the post

explanation.surface: An American writer who takes up a job in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with French post' reads as a diplomat abroad; split it, and it is a man from Normandy who sends letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, author of The Naked and the Dead.

clue.text: Good French drinking wine that's fortified

definitions.note: the phrase describes a thing (a place that's fortified), so it matches the noun

indicators.note: someone drinking takes a liquid inside

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A fine French tipple that has been fortified, like port or sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Fortified wine is a real thing, which hides that 'that's fortified' is the definition, a place rather than a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a bastion is a projecting part of a fortress, and by extension any stronghold.

clue.text: Perfume, rotten odour ultimately, time for incense

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the end letter of each word

parts.note: perfumE, rotteN, odouR: the last letters
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A complaint about perfume that smells rotten, burning time as if it were incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like the scented stick, fitting perfume and odour; it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, meaning to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym once the verb sense is seen: to incense someone is to make them furious.

clue.text: Wild West lawman, a petty war criminal

indicators.note: a criminal breaks the rules, so the letters break out of their order

explanation.surface: A frontier sheriff dismissed as a small-time war criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War criminal' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'criminal' is the signal acting on 'a petty war'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Wyatt Earp was a lawman of the Old West, famous for the gunfight at the O.K. Corral.

clue.text: Glue-stiffened cloth two males stuck together

indicators.note: things stuck together are joined, so the two animal words are set end to end

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two men stuck to each other by glue-stiffened fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Males' means male animals, not men; 'stuck' echoes the glue of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: buckram is coarse cloth stiffened with glue or size, used in bookbinding and hat-making.

clue.text: This part of stair is erect

definitions.text: This part of stair is erect

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the letters that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the last letter of stair, all of 'is', and the first two of erect

explanation.surface: A note on how stairs are built: this piece stands upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: of a step's two faces, the tread is flat and the answer is the upright one.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: the vertical board between two treads of a staircase is the part of the stair that stands erect.

clue.text: Fairly new parts Waugh cut?

indicators.note: to part something is to split it
a cut name is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the first name without its last letter
Evelyn Waugh, the English novelist, stands for his first name

explanation.surface: Asking whether Waugh's new book was cut fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waugh' stands for his first name, not the surname, which is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to share evenly is to share fairly, with equal portions.

clue.text: Wisdom built up legendary area?

parts.note: a saga is a legendary tale, used here as an adjective
a city is a built-up area; 'legendary' sits inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Wisdom accumulated over time in some fabled region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Built up' seems to go with wisdom, but it belongs to 'area', so the whole reads as a legendary built-up area.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sagacity is shrewd, practical wisdom.

clue.text: University lecture

definitions.meaning: a university in the English town of that name, west of London
a formal talk or recital; the French word lecture has the same sense

explanation.surface: A university lecture, seen from a student's timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'University' is a proper name here: Reading is a Berkshire town with its own university.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a place name standing for its university, and a public recital or lecture.

clue.text: Stirrer got raita mixed up

indicators.note: like a stirred dip, the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen spoon that has got the raita all mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Raita is an Indian yoghurt dip, so 'stirrer' reads as a spoon; it is a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the British sense: a stirrer is someone who stirs up trouble.

clue.text: I'm annoyed about people behind Polish national song

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way, so the exclamation is read backwards
the people stand behind, after, the other pieces

parts.note: a curse someone utters when irritated
to sand a surface is to polish it

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by people standing behind a Polish national anthem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish national song' reads as an anthem; the capital P hides the plain verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: this is Noël Coward's comic song about the English going out in the midday sun.

clue.text: Wish before dance ball

parts.note: to long for is to wish for
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Making a wish before going to a dance ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance ball' paints a ballroom; the ball here is a delivery in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term: a long hop is a short-pitched ball that bounces high and is easy to hit.

clue.text: A number one in Abba hit, health hazard!

indicators.note: the number one goes in, inside, the song title

explanation.surface: An Abba chart-topper denounced as a danger to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a chart position that suits 'hit', but it is a word for the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: asbestos fibres cause lung disease, making it a notorious health hazard.

clue.text: Familiar name, not so for burner

indicators.note: 'not so' means without SO, so those two letters are removed

parts.note: the two letters taken off the front

explanation.surface: A nickname that isn't so familiar after all, given to someone who burns things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads as a denial, but it tells you to drop the letters SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a briquet, or briquette, is a block of compressed coal dust made for burning.

clue.text: Still case incomplete after arrest of Romeo for murders

indicators.note: an incomplete word is missing its last letter

parts.note: a chest is a box or case
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A detective's frustration: the murder case still unfinished after Romeo is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: The police story makes 'case' a criminal case and 'arrest' a detention; here the case is a box, and it holds the letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to butcher people is to murder them brutally.

clue.text: African line crossed by an Indian

indicators.note: the line is crossed by the other letters, which lie on either side of it

explanation.surface: An African border line that an Indian traveller crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' is a person from one particular Indian state, which is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: an Angolan is a person from Angola in southern Africa.

clue.text: Filthy old measure

definitions.meaning: a traditional count of twelve dozen, 144

explanation.surface: A dirty old unit of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense survives in wholesale trade, where goods were counted in dozens of dozens.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: disgusting, and a count of 144 items.

clue.text: Birds I located in parts east of Idaho, finally

indicators.note: the I is located inside the parts
in an across answer east is to the right, so the parts come after the letter from Idaho
finally means at the end, so take the last letter

explanation.surface: A birder reporting sightings in the region east of Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as regions of the country; it is theatrical roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: orioles are brightly coloured songbirds.

clue.text: Old peacekeepers when safe go it alone: UN formed

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so the letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Old peacekeeping forces going solo once the UN was set up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is history in a nutshell: the older body was wound up when the United Nations was founded.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the League of Nations was the international body set up to keep the peace after the First World War.

clue.text: Animal lugged by the lugholes?

indicators.note: lugholes is British slang for ears, so the word is taken in by ear, as it sounds

explanation.surface: An animal hauled along by its ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lugholes' echoes 'lugged' and makes the ears sound like handles to drag by.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the toad is an amphibian.

clue.text: Covert operation as cry heard from protesting vegan?

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the cry is taken by its sound

parts.note: what a vegan might chant against meat

explanation.surface: A secret police operation posing as a vegan protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegan chant against beef sounds just like the police term for watching a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a stakeout is secret surveillance of a place, one kind of covert operation.

clue.text: Openers depend on this critical call

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Batsmen whose innings hinges on one crucial umpiring decision.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen; here they are things that open locks, which literally hang from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: keys are openers, and they depend, in the sense of hang, from this holder.

clue.text: Republican has broken you — told you so!

indicators.note: the Republican has broken into the other word, so it sits inside it

explanation.surface: A gloat after a Republican defeats you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation of someone proved right, as in 'There! What did I say?'
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: said with satisfaction, the word means 'I told you so!'

clue.text: Fiction at first avoided, reaches for novel — a classic perhaps?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter
an avoided letter is kept out, so it is removed from 'for'
novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the opening letter, which is the one to avoid

explanation.surface: Someone skipping fiction and reaching for a novel instead, perhaps a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'classic' both suggest books; the Classics are the five great British flat races, such as the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example with 'perhaps' to show it: each of the five Classics is one kind of horse race.

clue.text: Cast actor in a production designed for the outdoors?

definitions.note: the phrase describes the garment, a thing designed for the outdoors

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown about
a production makes something, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Casting an actor in an open-air play.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre words 'cast' and 'production' look like context for 'actor', but both signal the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description with a question mark: a waterproof coat is designed for wear outside.

clue.text: The obligation is on me to drink — absolutely!

parts.note: the duty is mine: I ought to

explanation.surface: Someone who feels duty-bound to have a drink, and heartily agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: This is old British slang, a play on 'I should say so', used to mean certainly, often ironically.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional idiom: the British exclamation means 'I should think so!', that is, absolutely.

clue.text: Musical setter?

definitions.meaning: the stage show set in 1960s Baltimore
something that fixes a hairstyle in place

explanation.surface: A crossword setter with a musical bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the usual word for a crossword compiler; here it is a product that sets a hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the title of a Broadway musical, and a spray that sets hair.

clue.text: Woman turned hose around opening of dirty trough to clean animals

indicators.note: a turned word faces the other way, so the hose is read backwards
the reversed hose goes around the letter that follows
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A farmer's wife turning a hose on a filthy trough to wash livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: The farmyard picture is apt, but the hose is not sprayed: it is a word that gets flipped and wrapped round a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a sheep-dip is a bath of insecticide that sheep are plunged through to clean their fleece.

clue.text: Fitting, with little to spare

definitions.meaning: deserved and fair, as a fitting reward is
barely, by a narrow margin, as in catching a train with seconds left

explanation.surface: Clothes that fit, but only barely.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the two halves one idea, a snug fit; they are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: fair or deserved, and only barely.

clue.text: Tread on rogue in group, fantasist

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits directly above it, so the tread comes before the rogue
the pair goes in, inside, the group

explanation.surface: Stepping on a scoundrel in a gang of dreamers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tread on' looks like one phrasal verb, to step on; split it, and 'on' just places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: a space cadet is someone with their head in the clouds, out of touch with reality.

clue.text: Old capital governed, tough

parts.note: a goon is a hired thug, a tough

explanation.surface: A former capital ruled with a firm hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' looks like an adjective about the rule; it is a noun, a heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital of Burma until 2005.

clue.text: One without scent bottles still

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the word for scentless holds the one

parts.note: with no nose, so unable to smell

explanation.surface: A person who cannot smell bottling a still, as if making spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottles' and 'still' conjure a distillery; 'still' is the adjective, quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: still means making no sound.

clue.text: Each day appended to this month, preferably

indicators.note: appended means added at the end, so the each and day letters follow the month

parts.note: inst., instant, is old business-letter shorthand for this month

explanation.surface: A diary rule: add each day to this month's schedule, if you would.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in reverse of the clue order: the month comes first, then the other two are tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A close synonym: 'I'd have tea instead' means I'd preferably have tea.

clue.text: Country in rift, about which unhappy

indicators.note: about means around, so the unhappy word goes around what came before

explanation.surface: A nation in the middle of an unhappy dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In rift' reads as a country divided; 'in' is literal letters, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Singapore is a city-state in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: A boy from Bamako, for example, standing to welcome a priest

indicators.note: in a down answer, standing up means reading from the bottom
to welcome someone is to take them in, so the phrase takes in the second A

parts.note: the welcomed A, taken in after the country
Bamako is the capital of Mali, so its people are an example of those from Mali

explanation.surface: A Malian boy getting to his feet to greet a visiting cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' shows the boy stands for any lad from Mali; 'standing' flips the whole string upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Dalai Lama is the chief priest, or lama, of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Many debts owed by policeman

indicators.note: by means beside, so the debts sit next to the policeman

parts.note: an IOU is a note of a debt owed

explanation.surface: A policeman in trouble over lots of unpaid debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owed by' tells a story about a debt-ridden officer, but 'by' is just a positioning word.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: copious means plentiful, in large numbers.

clue.text: Versatile — as cabaret?

definitions.meaning: with every feature you could want
a cabaret show literally offers song and dance throughout

explanation.surface: A cabaret act praised for being able to do everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a cabaret really is full of performers vocalising and moving to music.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase describes something with every possible feature, like a gadget that does everything.

clue.text: Brass, a pound on something irritating

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the pound comes before the irritant

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: Complaining that money, a pound here and there, is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' is British slang for money, which fits the pound; here it means a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the althorn is a valved brass instrument of the saxhorn family.

clue.text: Illness confined to jail, men treatable

indicators.note: something confined is locked inside, so the answer is locked inside the words that follow

parts.note: all of jail but the J, all of men, and the T of treatable

explanation.surface: A prison doctor assures inmates their illness can be treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confined to jail' fits the prison story too well to look like an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an ailment is an illness, usually a minor one.

clue.text: Choral work provided great piece of rock

explanation.surface: A choir piece that turns out to be a great rock song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great piece of rock' seems to continue the music; it is geology.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a massif is a compact block of mountains, a great mass of rock.

clue.text: Hence, day tricky

parts.note: THU is the calendar abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: A remark that the day ahead will therefore be difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Any day could do; only Thursday's short form fits the crossing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: thusly, a jokey form of thus, can mean in this way and so, hence.

clue.text: For example, the bit without intro

indicators.note: a word without its intro has lost its introduction, its first letter

parts.note: a particle is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: Cutting the introduction off a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is not filler: in grammar it is the definite one of its word class, so 'for example, the' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'the' is the definite article in English grammar.

clue.text: Gentleman positioned horizontally for prayer?

definitions.note: the phrase describes the person, one there for prayer

explanation.surface: A man lying flat on the floor, perhaps prostrated in prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition: the man is someone you would go to for prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a chaplain is a clergyman attached to a school, hospital or regiment, who leads prayers.

clue.text: Tea cups in — this material?

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in curved hands, so the tea holds IN inside itself

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Asking what tea cups are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cups' is the verb, holding a word, while the surface makes it the noun; the whole also asks what cups are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: fine porcelain is the material tea cups are traditionally made of.

clue.text: Put lid on alcoholic drink

definitions.meaning: to put a stop to something, as with a rumour

explanation.surface: Capping a bottle of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put lid on' is not about bottles: it means to put the lid on a plan, to squash it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to thwart or end something, and whisky from Scotland.

clue.text: National reporter's commitment

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word is taken as a reporter would say it

parts.note: a tie is something that binds you, a commitment

explanation.surface: A national newspaper's reporter showing dedication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here, a citizen of a country, not an adjective for the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: a person from Thailand is one country's national.

clue.text: Sitcom mainly about impassive individual

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so most of the word, minus its last letter
to turn about is to move around, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A situation comedy built around a deadpan character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning', which suits the sitcom story; it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stoic endures hardship without showing feeling.

clue.text: Chapter in English constitutes poetic lines on page

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the page is joined to the pieces around it

explanation.surface: A chapter of an English book made up of verse on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not assembled in clue order: the page letter slots in right after English.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an episode is one part, or chapter, of a longer story.

clue.text: Dry your hands when muddied

indicators.note: muddied water is stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to wipe your hands after getting them dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an instruction to wipe your hands; it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: in chemistry, anhydrous means containing no water.

clue.text: Overture OK having introduced girls to endless wine

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so OK takes the girls and wine inside
an endless word has had its end, its last letter, removed

explanation.surface: An overture approved because it brought some girls to an unlimited supply of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid has no room for an apostrophe, so the title is entered without one.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Fingal's Cave is Mendelssohn's concert overture, also called The Hebrides.

clue.text: As shot, it tumbled into river, in other words

indicators.note: tumbled letters have fallen out of order and are rearranged
the mixed letters go into, inside, the river

parts.note: the letters of these words rearranged
the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: Someone shot and falling into a river, explained another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As shot' looks like a description of the victim, but those words are letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase introduces a restatement, just as 'in other words' does.
